dtc.priority: Audit what ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Gemini and Perplexity currently state about each baby/kids client's recalled or reformulated SKUs, then fix the source pages and structured data behind the wrong answers. Trigger: Target recalled Up&Up baby wipes on June 4 (FDA found harmful bacteria) on top of a 2026 cluster of baby-product recalls — AI surfaces lag recalls badly, and under the Air Canada precedent the brand owns whatever its AI says about product safety and availability.

landscape.headline: Agentic Storefronts now default — Catalog data feeds AI answers directly
landscape.body: Shopify activated Agentic Storefronts by default for eligible US merchants on March 11, 2026, syndicating Catalog product data straight to ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, Google AI Mode and Gemini via API. Whatever attributes sit in Catalog are now what AI states about the product — so stale age-grading, materials, or safety attributes propagate instantly across every AI surface.

landscape.headline: 2026 product-liability wave treats chatbots as extensions of the brand
landscape.body: Following the Air Canada ruling, 2026 plaintiffs are pleading traditional product-liability theories — design defect, failure to warn, negligence — against companies whose AI gives wrong product facts. The brand, not the bot, absorbs the misrepresentation. A single hallucinated safety or ingredient fact on a kids' product is now direct legal exposure.

landscape.headline: AI now states product facts on far more queries — and gets attributions wrong
landscape.body: Commercial queries showing Google AI Overviews grew from 8% to 18.5% in a year (Semrush, 10M keywords). Perplexity and Gemini still hallucinate a meaningful share of source attributions. More AI-stated product facts means more surface area for an answer about your brand to be wrong.

landscape.headline: Baby-product recall cluster widens the gap between AI answers and reality
landscape.body: Target's June 4 Up&Up baby-wipes recall joins 2026 recalls of infant walkers, nursing pillows and swim floats. Recalled and reformulated SKUs are exactly where AI most dangerously lags ground truth for baby/kids brands — and where a wrong 'safe / in stock' answer is most damaging.

topIdea.title: Recall-and-Reformulation Accuracy Sweep for baby/kids Shopify brands

Sold as a one-time wedge, not a vague visibility retainer.

cannabis.priority: Audit and correct what ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity state about each client's legal status, THC/CBD content and licensed-state availability. Trigger: after the April 23 partial rescheduling, AI routinely overstates 'cannabis is now Schedule III' — true only for FDA-approved and state-licensed medical products, while adult-use stays Schedule I. The highest-liability error is AI surfacing a brand as available or legal in a state where it isn't licensed; brand-stated legal and health claims carry the exposure.

landscape.headline: DEA partial rescheduling: medical & FDA products to Schedule III, adult-use stays Schedule I
landscape.body: Acting AG Blanche's April 23 order (published April 28) moved FDA-approved marijuana products and state-licensed medical marijuana to Schedule III, with 280E tax relief for those licensees, while adult-use remains Schedule I. AI now broadly misstates this as a blanket 'cannabis is Schedule III' — wrong for adult-use, and a brand repeating it inherits the liability.

landscape.headline: Expedited DEA hearing on full rescheduling, June 29 – ~July 15
landscape.body: A DEA administrative hearing on whether to reschedule marijuana as a whole to Schedule III begins June 29 and concludes by ~July 15. The legal picture may shift again within weeks, so any AI answer or brand copy asserting a fixed federal status should be treated and labeled as a moving target.

landscape.headline: CA DCC emergency rule allows simultaneous adult-use + medical licenses
landscape.body: California's DCC announced (May 18) emergency regulations letting licensees hold separate adult-use and medical licenses at once, with a possible June 5 effective date; ~1,600 licensees are eligible. Dual-license operators must keep distinct Metrc accounts and books — and AI answers that blur which SKUs are medical vs adult-use can misrepresent what's legally for sale. [partially unverified: confirm final effective date]

landscape.headline: AI rarely surfaces dispensaries — so every mention must be correct
landscape.body: SOCi's 2026 index shows ChatGPT recommends just 1.2% of locations (Perplexity 7.4%, Gemini 11%) and cannabis visibility is declining. AI answers about cannabis skew toward legal status, science and regulatory questions — exactly where an error becomes compliance exposure. The job here isn't visibility; it's making the rare mention accurate and compliant.

topIdea.label: Compliance Accuracy Audit
topIdea.title: Legal-status & potency accuracy sweep for multi-state cannabis CPG
topIdea.body: For each brand, capture what ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity state about THC/CBD content, health claims, federal status and per-state availability; flag any answer that surfaces the brand as legal or buyable in an unlicensed state or repeats the blanket 'Schedule III' error; correct the source pages, COA data and structured data behind those answers; deliver a compliance-grade before/after proof report. Cite primary sources; never give legal advice.
